dedupe_keys.name: bikez eth mass cycling trajectory dataset

description: BikeZ-ETH is a set of high-resolution bicycle trajectories from a controlled mass-cycling experiment on a circular test track at the ETH Zurich Hönggerberg campus on 6 September 2024. Twenty-eight cyclists were filmed by drone for about 30 minutes while the number of riders on the track (6 to 22) and the lane width (2.5 and 3.75 m) were varied and the flow was disrupted, capturing free flow, disturbed flow and stop-and-go waves. The release holds nine 4K videos at 25 frames per second split into 21 sequences, object annotations, and frame-level Cartesian trajectories obtained by object detection, tracking and Kalman filtering. It was produced by the Institute for Transport Planning and Systems at ETH Zurich and described in Scientific Data (13:940, 23 April 2026). Coverage is a single site, one experiment, with 29,367 usable frames. Data are free on Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 (version 1.0 of 30 December 2025: TRAJECTORIES.zip 28 MB, VIDEOS.zip 27 GB), with the extraction code on GitHub under MIT. Caveats: the sample is small, the setting only partly naturalistic, and results may not generalise to urban traffic. The data support calibration of microscopic bicycle flow models, the bicycle fundamental diagram for capacity planning of cycle lanes and network flow studies, and complement naturalistic drone datasets such as TUMDOT-MUC.
